scope: Research and integration record for the thirteen supported target languages. Every integrated source below exists in a local source-data file. Current catalogue/report counts, rather than this document, describe generated card coverage.
policy: Use redistributable primary-source lexical material and retain source identities, licences, attribution, source annotations and pinned input provenance.

No proprietary application decks are used. At the user’s request, original model-assisted editorial translations and modern usage corrections supplement the open dictionaries; these are explicitly distinguished from source-attested alternatives.

Classifications must describe the target language. Verified source labels and defensible research-derived estimates must be distinguished explicitly; estimates need recorded methodology and must never be presented as verified labels. Do not transfer English levels to translations, invert Russian levels into English, convert general-frequency ranks alone to CEFR, or equate HSK/JLPT/TOPIK with CEFR.

A CEFR-labelled corpus is not itself a word-level classification. A defensible, transparently labelled estimation method may use graded-corpus evidence, subject to compatible source licences. Broad semantic topics and comparative dictionary concepts are not CEFR curricula.
Excluded or unverified candidates are not imported. Noncommercial restrictions are incompatible with this project's required commercial redistribution scope.
Source row, sense and form counts are not unique-word counts. Imported source classifications do not imply official certification or native-speaker review of every resulting card.

languageFindings.name: English

frequency.method: Match this target language's own original token ranks; retain gaps and report partial coverage. No rank is converted to CEFR.

cefr.finding: CEFR-J 1.6 supplies English A1-B2 headword/POS classifications; Octanove 1.0 supplies the publisher's C1/C2 supplement. Exact English lemma/POS matches only. These are source-assigned lexical classifications, not official CEFR certification or independent validation of every dictionary sense.

limitations: Aligned translation-table coverage varies by meaning and language; a missing form is not generated.
IDS contributes source concept/chapter categories, not CEFR classifications; one eligible source form is selected per concept.

excludedCandidates.name: GerVLPro (Michael, Hülsing and Horbach, LREC 2026)
excludedCandidates.license: No explicit redistribution licence: GitHub API license=null, no licence file in the complete reviewed repository tree, and no grant in README or TSV.
excludedCandidates.reason: Potentially suitable as explicitly Estimated productive-vocabulary classifications: source CEFR-labelled learner texts and normalized per-level shares provide evidence beyond general frequency rank. Integration is blocked by unverified redistribution rights, not by automatic methodology. No dataset has been saved into project inputs.
excludedCandidates.methodology: Manual lexical validity filtering follows extraction from graded German learner corpora. The released preferred classification is the first CEFR level whose normalized within-level frequency share reaches 12 percent. It is a research-derived estimate of productive lexical development, not expert verification of each sense. Other occurrence-level columns must not silently replace the preferred classification.

excludedCandidates.reason: The reviewed resources attach CEFR labels to learner/reference texts, paragraphs or sentences. They do not supply verified word/sense-level classifications. Even a permissively licensed corpus does not justify transferring its text level to every word.

jmdict.requirement: EDRDG section 4 requires a regular source update procedure and gives monthly updates for WWW dictionary servers as an example. Documentation and licence links must remain available with attribution.
jmdict.procedure: Periodically check upstream JMdict; run scripts/fetch-asian-vocabulary.py --refresh; review source and selection changes; rebuild the vocabulary; run relevant checks; distribute the reviewed update. No schedule or publication is created by this research record.

consideredAlternatives.name: wordfreq
consideredAlternatives.status: Permitted alternative corpus; not selected in this integration
consideredAlternatives.reason: Its normalized combined-corpus word ranks differ from the retained raw FrequencyWords token positions. Chinese enumeration includes Oversimplified Chinese representations rather than display-ready orthography, requiring normalization-aware dictionary matching. It is not a CEFR classification and must not silently replace or renumber current ranks.

requirements: Explicit permission for commercial redistribution and adaptation
Actual target-language lexical classifications, or defensible lexical estimates clearly distinguished from verified labels
No CEFR mapping based only on general-frequency rank
additionalEuropeanCefrReview.outcome: No additional dataset satisfying the licensing and provenance requirements was verified in this bounded primary-source search. GerVLPro was re-evaluated as a potentially suitable Estimated source, but its available repository has no verified redistribution licence. No additional level file or extraction script was created.
additionalEuropeanCefrReview.nextEvidenceNeeded: A source-specific open redistribution grant for an existing lexical list or defensible estimated classification, or another compatible target-language source. An unverified candidate must not be presented as unavailable worldwide or as a completed CEFR deck.

supplements.methodology: Individual sense review by the coding assistant (model-assisted semantic curation), not human or native-speaker review. Each assignment was selected by inspecting an exact English dictionary translation heading, part of speech, and competing senses. Categories use the existing project taxonomy. No headword-wide or automatic keyword-based category assignment is applied. Dictionary translations are unchanged; no additional translation or CEFR label is inferred. Parent sense topics are not used as evidence for these assignments because some source translation tables are nested under unrelated parent glosses.

Individual-sense review: model-assisted semantic curation by the coding assistant. Each assignment was selected using the exact English Wiktionary translation heading and part of speech in expanded-lexicon.json, with practical relevance to the named activity. Candidate headwords were only used for discovery; homonymous meanings were inspected separately and only the listed concept IDs receive these categories. Headword, meaning and POS are reproduced unchanged for provenance and validation. All selected concepts have a Turkish form and at least eight language forms in the source; no translation or missing form was invented. Shared actions receive multiple categories only where their exact sense is useful in each activity. Existing source attribution, license and per-concept evidence remain in expanded-lexicon.json. This is dictionary-derived semantic classification, not native-speaker review, proficiency grading or verification of every translation.

semanticReview.automaticTopicGuard: Raw Kaikki parent-sense topics are propagated only when the exact normalized translation-table heading matches a parent sense gloss; nesting alone has proven unreliable. Other assignments require individual-sense review.
semanticReview.formReviewPolicy: Use an attested alternative in the same source table or omit the mismatched form; do not generate a new translation.

qualityRevision.scope: All primary native forms in the 13-language input inventory receive systematic checks; flagged candidates are individually reviewed. This is not independent native-speaker certification of every meaning.
qualityRevision.parentheses: Remove round/fullwidth/square-bracket annotations from both prebuilt study faces. Preserve raw input snapshots, sense metadata and source attribution. Custom saved decks are not rewritten.
qualityRevision.levels: Retain published English/Russian assignments; fill all other target entries with visibly estimated native-language study bands. Native frequency is only one feature alongside meaning/domain, POS, register, lexical complexity, positive anchor guards and individually reviewed native-sense overrides. No rank-only labels, English level transfer or HSK/JLPT/TOPIK equivalence.
qualityRevision.frequency: Pin reviewed ordinary target senses before choosing a translation language; missing translations cannot fall back to another homonymous sense. Omit unsupported grammatical tokens without filling lower ranks. Original corpus ranks remain unchanged.
qualityRevision.editorial: Original modern, core and advanced vocabulary with one explicit meaning and 13 translations. Language-specific choices are reviewed separately; all editorial CEFR labels remain estimates.
